sanskrit: agre bṛhann uṣasām ūrdhvo asthān nirjaganvān tamaso jyotiṣāgāt | agnir bhānunā ruśatā svaṅga ā jāto viśvā sadmāny aprāḥ ||
english: Tall, he stood foremost at the dawns, risen up; having driven away the darkness he came with light. Agni, with his own bright, shining radiance, newborn, has filled all dwellings.

sanskrit: sa jāto garbho asi rodasyur agne cārur vibhṛta oṣadhīṣu | citraḥ śiśuḥ pari tamāṁsy aktūn pra mātṛbhyo adhi kanikradad gāḥ ||
english: Born as the embryo of Heaven and Earth, O Agni, cherished and lovely among the plants, a wondrous child, crying aloud above his mothers, he passed beyond the darkness and the night-seasons.

sanskrit: viṣṇur itthā paramam asya vidvāñ jāto bṛhann abhi pāti tṛtīyam | āsā yad asya payo akrata svaṁ sacetaso abhy arcanti atra ||
english: Viṣṇu knowing well his highest station thus guards the third realm where he was born, great. When they fashioned their own nourishment from his mouth, those of one mind came thither to adore him.

sanskrit: ata u tvā pitubhṛto janitrīr annāvṛdham prati caranty annaiḥ | tā īm praty eṣi punar anyarūpā asi tvaṁ vikṣu mānuṣīṣu hotā ||
english: Those who bore him with fuel, his mothers, move toward him grown strong with food, with offerings. He returns to them again in another form; thou art the Hotṛ among the human tribes.

sanskrit: hotāraṁ citraratham adhvarasya yajñasya-yajñasya ketuṁ ruśantam | pratyardhiṁ devasya-devasya mahnā śriyā tv agnim atithiṁ janānām ||
english: The Hotṛ of the sacrifice, driver of the bright chariot, the banner of every rite, gleaming bright, matching in greatness every god and every god — I praise Agni, the honoured guest of men.

sanskrit: sa tu vastrāṇy adha peśanāni vasāno agnir nābhā pṛthivyāḥ | aruṣo jātaḥ pada iḻāyāḥ purohito rājan yakṣīha devān ||
english: Wearing his beautiful, variegated garments, Agni stands at the navel of the earth. Ruddy, born at the station of Iḷā, as Purohita, O King, worship here the gods.

sanskrit: ā hi dyāvāpṛthivī agna ubhe sadā putro na mātarā tatantha | pra yāhy accho śato yaviṣṭhāthā vaha sahasye iha devān ||
english: For thou, O Agni, ever stretchest out toward both Heaven and Earth as a son toward his two mothers. Go forward to those who laud thee, O youngest god; then bring the gods hither, O powerful one.

sanskrit: piprīhi devām̐ uśato yaviṣṭha vidvām̐ ṛtūm̐r ṛtupate yajeiha | ye daivyā ṛtvijas tebhir agne tvaṁ hotṝṇām asy āyajiṣṭhaḥ ||
english: Gladden the gods who long for it, O youngest, knowing the seasons, O Lord of the Seasons, sacrifice here. Among the divine officiants, O Agni, thou art the most skilled in sacrifice among the Hotṛs.

sanskrit: veṣi hotram uta potraṁ janānām mandhātāsi draviṇodā ṛtāvā | svāhā vayaṁ kṛṇavāmā havīṁṣi devo devān yajatv agnir arhan ||
english: Thou seekest the Hotṛ office and also the Potṛ office among men; thou art the Mandhātṛ, the giver of riches, keeper of holy Order. With Svāhā let us make our oblations; let divine Agni, worthy, sacrifice to the gods.

sanskrit: ā devānām api panthām aganma yac chakanavāma tad anu pravoḻhum | agnir vidvān sa yajāt sed u hotā so adhvarān sa ṛtūn kalpayāti ||
english: We have come upon the path of the gods; what we are able we will carry forward along it. Agni, the all-knowing, let him sacrifice, for he is the Hotṛ; it is he who orders the rites and the seasons.

sanskrit: yad vo vayam prominaāma vratāni viduṣāṁ devā aviduṣṭarāsaḥ | agniṣ ṭad viśvam ā pṛṇāti vidvān yebhir devām̐ ṛtubhiḥ kalpayāti ||
english: If we have violated your ordinances, O gods, less knowing than those who know, Agni, all-knowing, fills all that up, he by whose seasonal rites he orders the gods.

sanskrit: yat pākatrā manasā dīnadakṣā na yajñasya manvate martyāsaḥ | agniṣ ṭad hotā kratuvid vijānan yajiṣṭho devām̐ ṛtuśo yajāti ||
english: What mortal men of simple mind and feeble understanding do not comprehend of the sacrifice — that Agni as Hotṛ, knowing the rites, most skilled in worship, understands, and he worships the gods in due order.

sanskrit: viśveṣāṁ hy adhvarāṇām anīkaṁ citraṁ ketuṁ janitā tvā jajāna | sa ā yajasvā nṛvatīr anu kṣāḥ spārhā iṣaḥ kṣumatīr viśvajanyāḥ ||
english: For the begetter begat thee as the splendid face and bright banner of all rites. Worship, bringing bounty over all lands, bringing desirable refreshments that strengthen, benefits for all peoples.

sanskrit: yaṁ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī yaṁ tvāpas tvaṣṭā yaṁ tvā sujanimā jajāna | panthām anu pravidvān pitṛyāṇaṁ dyumad agne samidhāno vi bhāhi ||
english: Thee whom Heaven and Earth begat, thee whom the Waters begat, thee whom Tvaṣṭṛ, the well-shaping craftsman, begat — knowing well the ancestral path, O Agni, blazing bright, shine forth resplendently.

sanskrit: ino rājann aratiḥ samiddho raudro dakṣāya suṣumām̐ adarśi | cikid vi bhāti bhāsā bṛhatāsiknīm eti ruśatīm apājan ||
english: The mighty Aratin, O King, blazing up, terrible in power, with skill, was seen in beauty. He shines forth conspicuously with his great radiance; driving away the dark one he moves toward the bright.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāṁ yad enīm abhi varpasā bhūj janayan yoṣām bṛhataḥ pitur jām | ūrdhvam bhānuṁ sūryasya stabhāyan divo vasubhir aratir vi bhāti ||
english: When by his form he overwhelmed the dark doe-antelope, begetting the daughter of the great Father, the glowing woman — holding up the sun's bright beam on high, Aratin shines forth with the treasures of heaven.

sanskrit: bhadro bhadrayā sacamāna āgāt svasāraṁ jāro abhy eti paścāt | supraketair dyubhir agnir vitiṣṭhan ruśadbhir varṇair abhi rāmam asthāt ||
english: The auspicious one, accompanied by the auspicious one, has come; the lover approaches his sister from behind. Spreading out with his well-marked, brilliant days, Agni with his shining colors has stood facing the darkness.

sanskrit: asya yāmāso bṛhato na vagnūn indhānā agneḥ sakhyuḥ śivasya | īḍyasya vṛṣṇo bṛhataḥ svāso bhāmāso yāmann aktavaś cikitre ||
english: His coursings, like the roarings of the great one, kindling the fire of the auspicious friend — of the praiseworthy bull, the great one who roars well — his flaming blazes, his night-gleams, shine in his going.

sanskrit: svanā na yasya bhāmāsaḥ pavante rocanānasya bṛhataḥ sudivas | jyeṣṭhebhir yas tejiṣṭhaiḥ krīḻumadbhir varṣiṣṭhebhir bhānubhir nakṣati dyām ||
english: His blazes roar like winds as he shines, the great one who illumines beautiful days; he who with his greatest, sharpest, most playful, most lofty radiances reaches even the sky.

sanskrit: asya śuṣmāso dadṛśānapaver jehamānasya svanayan niyudbhiḥ | pratnebhir yo ruśadbhir devatamodromi vi rebhadbhir aratir bhāti vibhvā ||
english: His gusts, of him who spreads out widely as he puffs and roars with his steeds — he who with his ancient gleaming, most divine, resonant radiances shines throughout as Aratin.

sanskrit: sa ā vakṣi mahi na ā ca satsi divaspṛthivyor aratir yuvatyoḥ | agniḥ sutuka sutukebhir aśvai rabhasvadbhīr rabhasvām̐ eha gamyāḥ ||
english: Carry the great one to us and sit with us, O Aratin, between the two young ones, Heaven and Earth. Let Agni, swift, with his swift, vigorous horses, come hither with vigor.

sanskrit: pra te yakṣi pra ta iyarmi manma bhuvo yathā vandyo no haveṣu | dhanvann iva prapā asi tvam agna iyakṣave pūrave pratna rājan ||
english: I worship thee, I send forth praise to thee, that thou mayst be worthy of honor in our invocations. Like a watering-place in the desert thou art, O Agni, for Pūru who desires to sacrifice, O ancient King.

sanskrit: yaṁ tvā janāso abhi saṁcaranti gāva uṣṇam iva vrajaṁ yaviṣṭha | dūto devānām asi martyānām antar mahāṁś carasi rocanena ||
english: Thee, whom men surround as cows approach a warm stall, O youngest one, thou art the messenger between the gods and mortals; thou roamest in between as the great one, through the shining realm.

sanskrit: śiśuṁ na tvā jenyaṁ vardhayantī mātā bibharti sacanasyamānā | dhanor adhi pravatā yāsi haryan jigīṣase paśur ivāvasṛṣṭaḥ ||
english: As a mother cherishes her noble child and makes him thrive, tending him carefully, thou descendest swiftly from the bow, O eager one, and streakest forth like a loosened animal.

sanskrit: mūrā amūra na vayaṁ cikitvā mahitvam agne tvam aṅga vitse | śaye vavriś carati jihvayādan rehyate yuvatim viśpatiḥ san ||
english: We are foolish and do not know, O wise Agni; thou thyself knowest thy own greatness well. He lies concealed, yet roams, eating with his tongue, and licks the young woman, being the lord of the folk.

sanskrit: kūcij jāyate sanayāsu navyo vane tasthau palito dhūmaketuḥ | asnātāpo vṛṣabho na pra veti sacetaso yam praṇayanta martāḥ ||
english: He is born ever-new among the ancient ones; he stands in the forest grey-haired, smoke-bannered. Like a bull whose thirst is unquenched he moves forward; him whom men of one mind lead on.

sanskrit: tanūtyajeva taskārā vānargū raśanābhir daśabhir abhy adhītām | iyaṁ te agne navyasī manīṣā yukṣvā rathaṁ na śucayadbhir aṅgaiḥ ||
english: Like thieves who hazard their bodies, the two who roam through the forest, have clothed themselves with ten ropes. Here, O Agni, is a newer hymn for thee; yoke thy chariot as it were with gleaming limbs.

sanskrit: brahma ca te jātavedas namaś ceyaṁ ca gīḥ sadam id vardhanī bhūt | rakṣā ṇo agne tanayāni tokā rakṣota nas tanvo aprayucchan ||
english: May this prayer and this reverence and this song be ever a source of increase to thee, O Jātavedas. Guard for us, O Agni, our children and offspring; protect our bodies without ceasing.

sanskrit: ekaḥ samudro dharuṇo rayīṇām asmad dhṛdo bhūrijanmā vi caṣṭe | siṣakty ūdhar niṇyor upastha utsasya madhye nihitam padaṁ veḥ ||
english: The one ocean, foundation of riches, with many births, surveys us from our hearts. He clings to the udder in the lap of the hidden waters; the station of the bird is set in the midst of the fountain.

sanskrit: samānaṁ nīḻaṁ vṛṣaṇo vasānāḥ saṁ jagmire mahiṣā arvatībhiḥ | ṛtasya padaṁ kavayo ni pānti guhā nāmāni dadhire parāṇi ||
english: Clad in the same abode, the bulls have come together with the mares. The poets guard the station of Holy Order; they have placed the hidden names beyond.

sanskrit: ṛtāyinī māyinī saṁ dadhāte mitvā śiśuṁ jajñatur vardhayantī | viśvasya nābhiṁ carato dhruvasya kaveś cit tantum manasā viyantaḥ ||
english: The two, possessed of holy order and of magic power, hold together; having met, they begat the child and nourish it — unwinding with the mind even the thread of the moving and the stationary, the navel of all the world.

sanskrit: ṛtasya hi vartanayaḥ sujātam iṣo vājāya pradivas sacante | adhīvāsaṁ rodasī vāvasāne ghṛtair annair vāvṛdhāte madhūnām ||
english: For the tracks of Holy Order attend upon the well-born one, upon the impulses that have come long ago, for vigor. Wearing their garment, the two worlds when praised increase together with ghee, with food, with sweetnesses.

sanskrit: sapta svasṝr aruṣīr vāvaśāno vidvān madhva uj jabhārā dṛśe kam | antar yeme antarikṣe purājā icchan vavrim avidat pūṣaṇasya ||
english: Eager, knowing, he has loudly called the seven ruddy sisters and raised them up with honey to be seen. He who was born of old, spanning the mid-air, seeking, found the hiding-place of Pūṣan.

sanskrit: sapta maryādāḥ kamayas tatakṣus tāsām ekām id abhy aṁhuro gāt | āyor ha skambha upamaysa nīḻe pathāṁ visargeṁ dharuṇeṣu tasthau ||
english: The poets fashioned seven boundaries; to one of these alone the wicked one approached. Standing in the nest of the highest of Āyu, at the branching of the paths, on the firm foundations.

sanskrit: asac ca sac ca parame vyoman dakṣasya janmann aditer upasthe | agnir ha naḥ prathamajā ṛtasya pūrva āyuni vṛṣabhaś ca dhenuḥ ||
english: Both the Non-existent and the Existent are in the highest firmament, in the birth of Dakṣa, in the lap of Aditi. Agni indeed is our firstborn of Holy Order, the bull and the cow in an earlier age of existence.

sanskrit: ayaṁ sa yasya śarmann avobhir agner edhate jaritābhiṣṭau | jyeṣṭhebhir yo bhānubhir ṛṣūṇām paryeti parivīto vibhāvā ||
english: This is he in whose shelter and with whose aid the praiser kindles the fire and wins his wish. He who, surrounded, goes about the seers with his greatest radiances, the far-shining one.

sanskrit: yo bhānubhir vibhāvā vibhāty agnir devebhir ṛtāvājasraḥ | ā yo vivāya sakhyā sakhibhyo 'parihvṛto atyo na saptiḥ ||
english: He who, far-shining, shines with his radiances, Agni, with the gods, keeper of holy order, unceasing, he who has won friendship from his friends, not turning aside, like a swift steed.

sanskrit: īśe yo viśvasyā devavīter īśe viśvāyur uṣaso vyuṣṭau | ā yasmin manā havīṁṣy agnāv ariṣṭarathaḥ skabhnāti śūṣaiḥ ||
english: He who commands all divine refreshment, who commands all life at the brightening of Dawn — in whose fire, all-sustaining, Ariṣṭaratha sets the oblations in mind, with his praises.

sanskrit: śūṣebhir vṛdho juṣāṇo arkair devām̐ acchā raghupatvā jigāti | mandros hotā sa juhvā yajiṣṭhaḥ sammiślo agnir ā jiharti devān ||
english: Increased by praises, delighting in the hymns, swift-flying he goes toward the gods. That joyful Hotṛ with his ladle, most skilled in sacrifice, Agni who mingles with them, draws the gods near.

sanskrit: tam usrām indraṁ na rejamānam agniṁ gīrbhir namobhir ā kṛṇudhvam | ā yaṁ viprāso matibhir gṛṇanti jātavedasaṁ juivaṁ sahānām ||
english: Glorify with songs and reverences that gleaming Agni who trembles like Indra, whom the inspired seers praise with their thoughts — Jātavedas, wielder of the oblation-ladle, who bears the burden.

sanskrit: saṁ yasmin viśvā vasūni jagmur vāje nāśvāḥ saptīvanta evaiḥ | asme ūtīr indravātatamā arvācīnā agna ā kṛṇuṣva ||
english: In whom all good things have assembled, as horses with swift steeds in the race — turn hither to us, O Agni, the aids that are most like those of Indra.

sanskrit: adhā hy agne mahnā niṣadyā sadyo jajñāno havyo babhūtha | taṁ te devāso anu ketam āyann adhāvardhanta prathamāsa ūmāḥ ||
english: For indeed, O Agni, by thy greatness, sitting present, straightway when born thou wert fit to be invoked. The gods followed thy will in that; the primal helpers then grew strong.

sanskrit: svasti no divo agne pṛthivyā viśvāyur dhehi yajathāya deva | sacemahi tava dasma praketair uruṣyā ṇa urubhir deva śaṁsaiḥ ||
english: Grant us, O Agni, welfare from sky and earth; grant us all life for the act of worship, O god. May we attend upon thy discernments, O wonder-worker; protect us, O god, with your broad protections.

sanskrit: imā agne matayas tubhyaṁ jātā gobhir aśvair abhi gṛṇanti rādhaḥ | yadā te marto anu bhogam ānaḍ vaso dadhāno matibhiḥ sujāta ||
english: These thoughts, O Agni, born for thee, praise the bounty with cows and horses. When a mortal follows after thy gift, O Vasu, bearing thy praises, O well-born one.

sanskrit: agnim manye pitaram agnim āpim agnim bhrātaraṁ sadam it sakhāyam | agner anīkam bṛhataḥ saparyaṁ divi śukraṁ yajataṁ sūryasya ||
english: I think of Agni as a father, I think of Agni as a kinsman, I think of Agni as ever a brother and friend. I worship the face of great Agni — bright, adorable, dwelling in the sun in the sky.

sanskrit: sidhrā agne dhiyo asme sanutrīr yaṁ trāyase dama ā nityahotā | ṛtāvā sa rohidaśvaḥ purukṣur dyubhir asmā ahabhir vāmam astu ||
english: Efficacious prayers that gain spoils are ours, O Agni, for him whom thou protectest at home, O everlasting Hotṛ. That keeper of holy order, red-horsed, rich in rain, may he have good fortune through his days and nights.

sanskrit: dyubhir hitam mitram iva prayogam pratnam ṛtvijam adhvarasya jāram | bāhubhyām agnim āyavo 'jananta vikṣu hotāraṁ ny asādayanta ||
english: With day-gifts set, like a friend useful for service, the ancient ritual priest, the lusty lover of the rite — the descendants of Āyu with their arms generated Agni and seated him as Hotṛ among the peoples.

sanskrit: svayaṁ yajasvā divi deva devān kiṁ te pākaḥ kṛṇavad apracetāḥ | yathāyaja ṛtubhir deva devān evā yajasvā tanvaṁ sujāta ||
english: Sacrifice thou thyself to the gods in heaven, O god; what can the simple-minded, thoughtless one accomplish for thee? As thou hast sacrificed to the gods in the seasons, O god, so sacrifice, O well-born one, for thyself.

sanskrit: bhavā no agne 'vita uta gopā bhavā vayaskṛd uta no vayodhāḥ | rāsvā ca naḥ sumaho havyadātiṁ trāsvota nas tanvo aprayucchan ||
english: Be our protector, O Agni, and our guardian; be our strengthener of vigor and our nourisher. And grant us the gift of oblation-bearing, O greatly good one; protect us and our bodies without ceasing.

sanskrit: pra ketunā bṛhatā yāty agnir ā rodasī vṛṣabho roravīti | divaś cid antām̐ upamām̐ ud ānaḻ apām upasthe mahiṣo vavardha ||
english: Agni moves forward with his great banner; the bull roars filling the two worlds. He has reached even the highest limits of the sky; the great one has grown mighty in the lap of the waters.

sanskrit: mumoda garbho vṛṣabhaḥ kakudmān asremā vatsaḥ śimīvām̐ arāvīt | sa devatāty udyatāni kṛṇvan sveṣu kṣayeṣu prathamo jigāti ||
english: The crested bull, as the embryo, rejoiced; the calf, never resting, powerful, cried aloud. He, performing deeds surpassing those of the gods, goes first to his own abodes.

sanskrit: ā yo mūrdhānam pitror arabdha ny adhvare dadhire sūro arṇaḥ | asya patmann aruṣīr aśvabudhnā ṛtasya yonau tanvo juṣanta ||
english: He who has seized upon the head of his two parents — at the rite the flood of the sun has been laid down. On his flight, the ruddy mares rooted in horses delight in the womb of holy order, in their own forms.

sanskrit: uṣā-uṣo hi vaso agra eṣi tvaṁ yamayom abhavo vibhāvā | ṛtāya sapta dadhiṣe padāni janayan mitraṁ tanve svāyai ||
english: For, O Vasu, thou goest to the front of each dawn; thou wast the far-shining presence of the two Yamas. Thou settest seven stations for holy order, engendering Mitra for thine own self.

sanskrit: bhuvaś cakṣur maha ṛtasya gopā bhuvo varuṇo yad ṛtāya veṣi | bhuvo apāṁ napāj jātavedas bhuvo dūto yasya havyaṁ jujoṣaḥ ||
english: Thou hast become the eye of the great Ṛta, the guardian; thou hast become Varuṇa when thou seekest holy order. Thou hast become the Son of the Waters, O Jātavedas; thou hast become the messenger of him whose oblation thou dost favor.

sanskrit: bhuvo yajñasya rajasaś ca netā yatrā niyudbhiḥ sacase śivābhiḥ | divi mūrdhānaṁ dadhiṣe svarṣāṁ jihvām agne cakṛṣe havyavāham ||
english: Thou hast become the leader of the sacrifice and of the expanse, where thou art present with thy benevolent teams. Thou hast set thy head in heaven, winning the sun; O Agni, thou hast made thy tongue the bearer of the oblation.

sanskrit: asya tritaḥ kratuṇā vavre antar icchan dhītim pitur evaim parasya | sacasyamānaḥ pitror upasthe jāmi bruvāṇa āyudhāni veti ||
english: Trita, within the cave, by the will of this one, seeking the intelligence, the tracks of the far Father, being helped, in the lap of his two parents, calling upon his kin, goes to fetch weapons.

sanskrit: sa pitryāṇy āyudhāni vidvān indreṣita āptyo abhy ayudhyat | triśīrṣāṇaṁ saptaraśmiṁ jaghanvān tvāṣṭrasya cin niḥ sasṛje trito gāḥ ||
english: Knowing the paternal weapons, spurred by Indra, the Waters' son fought against the enemy. Having slain the three-headed one of the seven rays, Trita released even the cattle of Tvaṣṭṛ's son.

sanskrit: bhūrīd indra udinakṣantam ojo 'vābhinat satpatir manyamānam | tvāṣṭrasya cid viśvarūpasya gonām ācakrāṇas trīṇi śīrṣā parā vark ||
english: Much did Indra surpass the rising might; the lord of the good overwhelmed the proud one. Even of Tvaṣṭṛ's son Viśvarūpa, while seizing his cattle, he cut away the three heads.

sanskrit: āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvas tā na ūrje dadhātana | mahe raṇāya cakṣase ||
english: O Waters, you are truly sources of well-being; grant us strength and vigor for great joy and to behold the great.

sanskrit: yo vaḥ śivatamo rasas tasya bhājayateiha naḥ | uśatīr iva mātaraḥ ||
english: Of your most auspicious essence grant us a share here, like eager mothers.

sanskrit: tasmā araṁ gamāma vo yasya kṣayāya jinvatha | āpo janayathā ca naḥ ||
english: Let us hasten to you, for whose abode you quicken us; O Waters, generate us.

sanskrit: śaṁ no devīr abhiṣṭaya āpo bhavantu pītaye | śaṁ yor abhi sravantu naḥ ||
english: May the divine Waters be auspicious for our protection, for our drinking; may they flow on us for well-being and happiness.

sanskrit: īśānā vāryāṇāṁ kṣayantīś carṣaṇīnām | apo yācāmi bheṣajam ||
english: Ruling over precious things, presiding over men — I ask the Waters for healing.

sanskrit: apsu me somo abravīd antar viśvāni bheṣajā | agniṁ ca viśvaśambhuvam ||
english: Within the waters Soma has declared to me all remedies, and Agni, who brings welfare to all.

sanskrit: āpaḥ pṛṇīta bheṣajaṁ varūthaṁ tanve mama | jyok ca sūryaṁ dṛśe ||
english: O Waters, provide the healing balm, the protection for my body, so that I may long look upon the sun.

sanskrit: idam āpaḥ pra vahata yat kiṁ ca duritam mayi | yad vāham abhiduroha yad vā śepa utānṛtam ||
english: O Waters, carry away whatever evil is in me, whatever wrong I may have done, or whatever curse or falsehood.

sanskrit: āpo adyānv acāriṣaṁ rasena sam agasmahi | payasvān agna ā gahi tam mā saṁ sṛja varcasā ||
english: I have gone today with the Waters; we have mingled with their essence. O Agni, rich in milk, come hither; unite me with splendor.

sanskrit: o cit sakhāyaṁ sakhyā vavṛtyāṁ tiraḥ purū cid arṇavaṁ jaganvān | pitur napātam ā dadhīta vedhā adhi kṣami prataraṁ dīdhyānaḥ ||
english: Yamī speaks: I would surely turn a friend toward friendship, though he has passed over many floods. The ordainer should establish us as the grandson's line of the Father, thinking of further offspring upon the earth.

sanskrit: na te sakhā sakhyaṁ vaṣṭy etat salakṣmā yad viṣurūpā bhavāti | mahas putrāso asurasya vīrā divo dhartāra urviyā pari khyan ||
english: Yama speaks: Thy friend does not wish for this friendship — that she who is of the same sign should become of a different form. The heroic sons of the great Asura, who uphold the sky, look out over the wide world.

sanskrit: uśanti ghā te amṛtāsa etad ekasya cit tyajasam martyasya | ni te mano manasi dhāyy asme janyuḥ patis tanvam ā viviśyāḥ ||
english: Yamī speaks: Indeed the immortals desire this, that progeny of this one mortal might arise. Let thy mind be set in my mind; a husband should enter the body of his wife.

sanskrit: na yat purā cakṛmā kad dha nūnam ṛtā vadanto anṛtaṁ rapema | gandharvo apsv apyā ca yoṣā sā no nābhiḥ paramaṁ jāmi tan nau ||
english: Yama speaks: What we have not done before, how should we do it now? We who speak of holy order — should we speak falsehood? Gandharva is in the waters and the watery maiden — she is our highest tie of kinship, she is our utmost bond.

sanskrit: garbhe nu nau janitā dampatī kar devas tvaṣṭā savitā viśvarūpaḥ | nakir asya pra minanti vratāni veda nāv asya pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Yamī speaks: Surely the divine Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ the all-shaped, will make us husband and wife in the womb. None violates his ordinances; both Earth and Heaven know of this for us.

sanskrit: ko asya veda prathamasyāhnaḥ ka īṁ dadarśa ka iha pra vocat | bṛhan mitrasya varuṇasya dhāma kad u brava āhano vīcyā nṝn ||
english: Yama speaks: Who knows of the first day? Who has seen it? Who would proclaim it here? Great is the ordinance of Mitra and Varuṇa. What would you say, O Yamī, to men with impunity?

sanskrit: yamasya mā yamyaṁ kāma āgan samāne yonau sahaśeyyāya | jāyeva patye tanvaṁ riricyāṁ vi cid vṛheva rathyeva cakrā ||
english: Yamī speaks: The longing for Yama has come upon Yamī, to lie together in the same womb. As a wife opens her body to her husband — I would spread apart like the wheels of a chariot.

sanskrit: na tiṣṭhanti na ni miṣanty ete devānāṁ spaśa iha ye caranti | anyena mad āhano yāhi tūyaṁ tena vi vṛha rathyeva cakrā ||
english: Yama speaks: These spies of the gods who wander here do not stand still, they do not close their eyes. Go quickly elsewhere, Yamī, not to me; spread apart with him like the wheels of a chariot.

sanskrit: rātrībhir asmā ahabhir daśasyet sūryasya cakṣur muhur un mimīyāt | divā pṛthivyā mithunā sabandhū yamīr yamasya bibhṛyād ajāmi ||
english: Yamī speaks: With nights and with days she should serve him; let the eye of the sun open again and again. May Yamī, twin-born, related as kin to Yama, bear what is non-kin between Heaven and Earth.

sanskrit: ā ghā tā gacchān uttarā yugāni yatra jāmayaḥ kṛṇavann ajāmi | upa barbṛhi vṛṣabhāya bāhum anyam icchasva subhage patim mat ||
english: Yama speaks: Later ages shall come when those of the same kin will do what is not kin. O fortunate one, stretch out thy arm to the bull; seek thyself another husband, not me.

sanskrit: kim bhrātāsad yad anātham bhavāti kim u svasā yan nirṛtir nigacchāt | kāmamūtā bahv etad rapāmi tanvā me tanvaṁ sam pipṛgdhi ||
english: Yamī speaks: What use is a brother if she remains without refuge? What use is a sister when Nirṛti comes upon her? Smitten by longing I speak out much of this: unite thy body with my body.

sanskrit: na vā u te tanvā tanvaṁ sam papṛcyām pāpam āhur yaḥ svasāraṁ nigacchāt | anyena mat pramudasiḥ kalpayasva na te bhrātā subhage vaṣṭy etat ||
english: Yama speaks: I shall not unite my body with thy body. They call it evil when a man goes to his sister. Arrange for thyself pleasures with another, not me; thy brother, O fortunate one, does not desire this.

sanskrit: bato batāsi yama naiva te mano hṛdayaṁ cāvidāma | anyā kila tvāṁ kakṣyeva yuktam pari ṣvajāte libujeva vṛkṣam ||
english: Yamī speaks: Alas, alas, O Yama — we have not found out either thy mind or thy heart. Surely some other woman clasps thee as it were a girth on a yoked horse, as a creeper embraces a tree.

sanskrit: anyam ū ṣu tvaṁ yamy anya u tvām pari ṣvajāte libujeva vṛkṣam | tasya vā tvam mana icchā sa vā tavādhā kṛṇuṣva saṁvidaṁ subhadrām ||
english: Yama speaks: Let another clasp thee, Yamī, and let another clasp him as a creeper clasps a tree. Seek his mind, or let him seek thine; make a good compact together.
